name: Electronics Basics
description: From atomic structure to electric power. Choose the correct answer for each question.

questions.prompt: Which particle has a negative electric charge?
Which particle has a positive electric charge?
What does the valence band contain?
In which band can electrons move freely through a material?
What is the band gap?
What happens to the valence and conduction bands in a typical metal?
choices: They are separated by a large gap

questions.prompt: Why is copper a good conductor?
choices: Its electrons can move through the material
questions.answer: Its electrons can move through the material

questions.prompt: With no applied voltage, what is the net current in an ordinary copper wire?
choices: It flows both ways at 1 A

questions.prompt: Why does rubber normally act as an insulator?
choices: Very few electrons are free to move
questions.answer: Very few electrons are free to move

questions.prompt: Which material is normally a good electrical conductor?
Which material is normally an electrical insulator?
Why can ordinary tap water conduct electricity?
choices: Its protons are free in metal

questions.prompt: Which statement about plastic is correct?
choices: It has electrons, but very few can move freely
questions.answer: It has electrons, but very few can move freely

questions.prompt: In a metal circuit, which way do electrons drift through the external wires?
Which direction represents conventional current in the external circuit?
Which current direction is normally shown on circuit diagrams?
What does electric current measure?
choices: Charge passing a point per second
questions.answer: Charge passing a point per second

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electric current?
A current of 1 A means how much charge passes each second?
What happens to charge carriers as they pass through a resistor?
choices: They continue through while transferring energy
They permanently stop at its entrance
questions.answer: They continue through while transferring energy

questions.prompt: How should an ammeter be connected to measure current through a resistor?
How should a voltmeter be connected to measure voltage across a resistor?
choices: In place of the power supply

questions.prompt: Before measuring resistance with a multimeter, what should you do?
choices: Put the meter in current mode
